name: Lienz
kurzbeschreibung: The sunny district capital of Osttirol, nestled between the Lienzer Dolomiten and the Isel.
beschreibung:
Overview

Lienz is the sun-drenched capital of the Lienz district and the vibrant cultural and economic hub of East Tyrol. Situated at an altitude of 673 metres at the confluence of the glacial Isel and Drau rivers within an expansive mountain basin, the picturesque town nestles beneath the sheer limestone spires of the Lienz Dolomites. Home to approximately 12,000 residents, Lienz masterfully unites alpine mountain prowess with a southern, Mediterranean lifestyle. Enjoying over 2,070 hours of sunshine annually, living palms gracing its colourful central square, and bustling outdoor café terraces, Lienz is celebrated as Austria's "Sun City". Historic Bruck Castle, urban lifts, and access to the Hohe Tauern National Park establish Lienz as an extraordinary destination.

History

Settlement in the basin dates back millennia, flourishing during antiquity when the nearby Roman city of Aguntum thrived just east of today's town. Lienz first appeared in historical records in 1022 under the name Luenzina. In the 13th century, the powerful Counts of Gorizia designated Lienz their permanent seat of residence, granting town rights in 1242 and constructing imposing Bruck Castle overlooking the valley. Following the extinction of the Gorizian line around 1500, Lienz passed to Emperor Maximilian I and the Habsburg monarchy. The late-Gothic parish church of Saint Andrew contains the Gorizian burial crypts and moving memorial chapel frescoes by master Albin Egger-Lienz. In the modern era, Lienz blossomed into an educational and commercial beacon hosting international sports events.

Getting There

Lienz serves as East Tyrol's primary multimodal transport junction. Motorists arrive from Carinthia via the B100 Drautal road from Spittal an der Drau or enter from South Tyrol and Italy traversing the Puster Valley along the B100. From North Tyrol and Salzburg, the high-alpine Felbertauern Road (B108) cuts through the mountains via Mittersill and Matrei directly into town. Lienz railway station is served frequently by ÖBB regional and express trains connecting Klagenfurt and Fortezza/Franzensfeste. It also serves as the principal hub for comprehensive VVT regional buses linking all surrounding alpine valleys.

Tips

A tour of Bruck Castle is an absolute must: this medieval residence houses the Museum of Lienz featuring the world's premier collection of works by expressionist painter Albin Egger-Lienz alongside a Romanesque dual-level chapel. In town, the central Hauptplatz with the historic Liebburg castle invites leisurely strolls. Thrill seekers will love the Osttirodler alpine coaster on Mount Hochstein, descending 2.7 kilometres on tracks overlooking the city. Modern cable cars transport visitors onto the sunny Zettersfeld plateau, rewarding skiers and hikers with breathtaking 360-degree panoramas of the jagged Lienz Dolomites.
